# PRD 001: pij community

**Schema**: pij/prd · **Source**: 001-pij-community.dd.json · **Sections**: 8

<a id="meta"></a>

## Meta

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| title | PRD 001: pij community |
| status | draft |
| updated | 2026-11-04 |
| owner | pij-far-jackal |
| summary | A pij community is a project's agents operating as one cohesive fleet across many concurrent tasks. Its directory names every role, specialist and general, with its scope, holders, memory and outputs, so roles outlive seats and the community builds knowledge over time. |

<a id="why"></a>

## Why

Splitting work across focused seats keeps each context small. Small contexts make agents sharper and faster and cost less, because cost grows roughly with the square of the context. Today pij knows a handful of roles (prime, pm, pa, worker), and projects improvise specialists: brief files in one project, inline prompts that vanish in another. A specialist's knowledge dies with its seat, results are buried in messages, and nothing tells a coder that Docker work belongs to someone else. A community directory makes roles durable: a role outlives its seats, its knowledge grows across them, and work and results flow through it.

<a id="actors"></a>

## Actors

| id | name | need |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a-prime | prime | An operating picture of the community and prompts on what to fix next. |
| a-pm | pm | To staff its own work with coders and reviewers and route owned work to specialists. |
| a-pa | pa | To keep seats healthy without losing what they learned. |
| a-worker | worker seat | To be told its job, what it may touch, and where to send work it does not own. |
| a-requester | requester | To get a result back in the way it chose, without stalling. |
| a-jordan | operator | A fleet that gets better at its project over time and costs less. |

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

| id | goal |
| --- | --- |
| g-1 | A role outlives the seats that hold it. |
| g-2 | Knowledge accumulates per role, in git, indexed by flowspace. |
| g-3 | Owned work reaches its owner without anyone policing it. |
| g-4 | Results are durable records, not messages. |
| g-5 | The prime runs the community from one view that tells it what to do next. |

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non goals

| id | text |
| --- | --- |
| n-1 | Cross-machine communities. Out of scope, but nothing here may block them (req-17). |
| n-2 | Copying transcripts between machines; flowspace already holds conversation history. |
| n-3 | Permission enforcement between roles. |
| n-4 | pij starting or reviving seats on its own. |
| n-5 | Tracking seats lent between projects. |

| req-02 | Directory files live on the governance branch | Role definitions, role memory, outputs, the routing table and external entries live under `&lt;government-root&gt;/community/`. | req-03 | pij is the only writer, and never touches anyone else's edits | Directory files are written only through pij verbs. pij writes the JSON into the standing governance worktree, runs `ddocs validate` and `ddocs build` by absolute path, and commits only the paths it wrote, with `git add -- &lt;paths&gt;` then `git commit --only -- &lt;paths&gt;`. It uses no plumbing that moves the branch under a checkout, and it refuses when a path it is about to write carries an edit it did not make, so it never stages, commits, overwrites or reverts anyone else's edits. The store keeps a pointer (project id, repo-relative path, commit). pij never pushes. A missing `ddocs` gives a named refusal, and `just doctor` reports which ddocs pij uses.
